chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, raising it from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I dislike praying in their mosques.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not dislike it. There is no mosque built except that it is built upon the grave of a Prophet or a successor of a Prophet who was killed, and a sprinkle of his blood hit that spot. Therefore, Allah loved that He be remembered in it. So perform in it the obligatory [prayer] and the optional [prayers], and pay back in it what has passed you by [of missed prayers].'

key_terms.مَسَاجِدِهِمْ: Their mosques (referring to the mosques of the general Muslims or specific sects)

ai.seo_question: Why should one pray in the mosques of the general Muslims according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates praying in the mosques of the general Muslims by linking their sanctity to the graves of Prophets and Imams, asserting that a 'sprinkle of their blood' upon the site renders it a place where Allah is remembered. This hadith provides the theological basis for the Shia practice of visiting shrines (Ziyarat) and praying within them, emphasizing that the presence of the righteous deceased sanctifies the space regardless of the builders' identity. Consequently, the Imam instructs the narrator to perform both obligatory and voluntary prayers there, including making up missed prayers, thereby encouraging active worship rather than avoidance.
